Academia for Social Responsibility and the Common Good at Duke
description: Duke Academia for Social Responsibility and the Common Good (DASRCgood) is a community of graduate and professional students committed to exploring how academia can serve the public good. We foster interdisciplinary dialogue to understand how diverse fields—ranging from science and public health to policy, law, and the humanities—can contribute to a more just and equitable society. name: Academic Resource Center
description: We know you are already smart, but why stop there? The Academic Resource Center (ARC) is here so you can maximize your capabilities as an undergraduate student, and get the most out of your Duke experience.

name: Adopt A Grandparent
description: Adopt a Grandparent is a student community service organization of students who volunteer with the elderly, many of whom reside at nursing homes and rehabilitation centers close to Duke University. The mission of AAG is to provide disabled and institutionalized senior citizens with social and emotional support, to foster the formation of positive social relationships between senior citizens and Duke students, and to encourage understanding and appreciation of the senior citizens in our community, especially those who lack social support and financial resources.

name: Advanced Degree Medical Affairs Club at Duke
description: The mission of ADMAC is to educate its members about career paths in medical affairs and the pharmaceutical industry through presentations and networking with Duke alumni and professionals in the field and other industry service positions.

name: Advancing Representation in Consulting
description: The mission of the organization is to provide resources, education, and real-world consulting opportunities to first-generation, low-income, minority, and women students at Duke University, aiming to create a more inclusive consulting environment and address inequities in professional opportunities. Additionally, the organization seeks to apply consulting skills to support local businesses and nonprofits in Durham, fostering community engagement and real-world impact.

name: Agapé Campus Christian Fellowship
description: To provide undergrad and graduate students at Duke with a loving and encouraging space for bible study, worship, prayer, and fellowship.

name: AI Competition Club
description: Promote student and university excellence through AI & data science competitions Specifically the club strives to: Host competitions Compete against other universities Win industry competitions With the benefits of: Applying learning through practice Relationship building and networking within and outside the program and department Win awards and recognition for members, the program, and the university

name: AI in Business at Duke
description: Empowering Duke students to harness artificial intelligence for all business ambitions.

name: All of the Above
description: All of the Above presents a show annually including a series of anonymous monologues written, performed, and directed by Duke women about life at Duke. All of the Above hopes to not only raise awareness of gender inequity on campus, but also to celebrate the many facets of the Duke woman in a rare theatrical setting. The Production Team of All of the Above must ensure the annual performance continues and upholds the values of the 2003 Duke Women's Initiative, giving a voice to all women on campus.

name: Allied Scholars for Animal Protection at Duke
description: Allied Scholars for Animal Protection (ASAP) is a national program that fosters student organizations for animal advocacy, with chapters at multiple leading schools like MIT, Harvard, Yale, etc. The ASAP chapter at Duke aims to raise awareness about animal welfare issues in the modern agricultural industry and encourage more compassionate and sustainable choices on campus. We will achieve this through educational events, tabling, outreach activities, and collaboration with other student groups to build a more informed and engaged community. name: Alpha Kappa Alpha Sorority, Inc.
description: The purpose of the Iota Mu Chapter is to cultivate and encourage high scholastic and ethical standards, to promote unity and friendship among college women, to study and help alleviate problems concerning girls and women in order to improve their social stature, to maintain a progressive interest in college life, and to be of service to all mankind as stated in the Constitution and Bylaws of Alpha Kappa Alpha Sorority, Incorporated┬«.

name: alpha Kappa Delta Phi
description: Our mission is to provide sisterhood among women, and to promote scholarship, leadership and Asian awareness in the University and community. Further, to provide a support group for those in their times of need and to encourage the making of successful women.

name: Alpha Kappa Psi Business Fraternity
description: To create a network of talented, motivated, business-minded students and alumni that will provide mentorship and programming to Duke undergraduates and work together to plan and launch social entrepreneurial projects.

name: Alpha Phi Alpha Fraternity Inc. (Kappa Omicron)
description: Alpha Phi Alpha Fraternity, Inc. develops leaders, promotes brotherhood and academic excellence, while providing service and advocacy for our communities. The Kappa Omicron Chapter has continuously worked to uphold these standards since the Chapter's chartering on Sunday, December 7, 1975.

name: Alpha Phi Omega
description: The official purpose of the Fraternity is to assemble college students in a National Service Fraternity in the fellowship of principles derived from the Scout Oath and Scout Law of the Boy Scouts of America; to develop Leadership, to promote Friendship, and to provide Service to humanity; and to further the freedom that is our national, educational, and intellectual heritage.

name: Alpha Pi Omega Sorority Inc.
description: The mission of Alpha Pi Omega Sorority, Inc. is to create a strong sisterhood that will serve as a support for college women in today's society. The sisterhood shall support its members in their individual journeys towards a balanced life. The Alpha Pi Omega woman will always strive for greater scholarship, honesty, leadership, service, and personal integrity. The Sorority will work to preserve our Native American traditions, for through celebration and practice of our cultural and spiritual heritage, we become one with each other.

name: American Chemical Society Chapter
description: We aim to provide a space for chemistry majors to network about each other, learn more about the chemistry major, and discover chemistry opportunities and careers beyond Duke University.

name: American Futures Institute
description: The purpose of the organization is to give Duke students unique opportunities to explore the intersection of business with public policy and politics. We strive to teach our members important problem-solving skills that they can use to succeed on client projects and to succeed in making a difference in real world public policy for years to come.

name: American Grand Strategy
description: To prepare the next generation of national security strategists by studying past generations and interacting with current leaders.

name: American Lung Cancer Screening Initiative at Duke
description: The American Lung Cancer Screening Initiative (ALCSI) is a non-profit organization that is composed of a team of over 70 doctors and students working to increase awareness of lung cancer and lung cancer screening in communities across the country. Our mission is to improve the rate of lung cancer screenings for high-risk patients and reduce the rate of lung cancer through outreach efforts. By working with cities, local and national governments, and other organizations, ALCSI raises awareness for lung cancer and lung cancer screening. name: American Medical Women's Association Undergraduate Chapter
description: AMWA will be an organization that supports female pre-medical students at Duke. It will serve as both a welcoming community and a resource for members. AMWA will help to connect members to research, volunteer, shadowing, advising, and networking opportunities.

name: American Society of Civil Engineers
description: The American Society of Civil Engineers student chapter at Duke University is a student-run organization that enhances the experience of civil and environmental engineering students through guest lectures, opportunities to connect with industry professionals, mentorship, and various independent projects. Duke ASCE serves as the bridge to connecting students with the highly recognized international society of professional civil engineers. Our local chapter holds monthly general body meetings and invites professors of the department, as well as corporate speakers to connect with student members

name: Amnesty International
description: Amnesty International's vision is of a world in which every person enjoys all of the human rights enshrined in the Universal Declaration of Human Rights and other international human rights instruments. In pursuit of this vision, Amnesty International's mission is to undertake research and action focused on preventing and ending grave abuses of these rights.

name: Arabic Debate Club at Duke
description: The Duke Arabic Debate Club is dedicated to fostering an intellectual platform for Arabic-speaking students to engage in structured debate and meaningful dialogue. Our mission is to promote critical thinking, cultural exchange, and rhetorical skills in the Arabic language, while encouraging respect for diverse perspectives. Through debate and discussion, we aim to enhance participants' fluency, broaden their understanding of global and regional issues, and contribute to the vibrant academic and cultural community at Duke University.

name: Arnold Air Society; Kevin J. McManus Squadron
description: To build strong officers for the United States Air Force through our professional, honorary, service organization.

name: Arts Annex
description: The Arts Annex is a hub for student creativity, home to rehearsal, studio art, and programming spaces for student artists and organizations. The Arts Annex makes the arts accessible to all Duke students by providing increased studio arts resources, enhanced programming, and a welcoming environment that inspires self-expression, exploration, and collaboration. The Arts Annex is operated by Venue and Production Management, within Campus Life and Student Affairs. Check the events page for upcoming programs and to see when we are open! If you are interested in working with or planning an event at

name: Asian American Theater
description: Duke Asian American Theatre is an organization founded by Rachel Whitney (c/o 2014) in order to support and highlight Asian American representation in theatre. This organization will be focused on providing a space for Asian American students interested in theatre and will work to promote Asian American playwrights, actors, and technicians. However, this is an inclusive space for everyone and anyone.

name: Asian Athletes Network
description: Our mission is to empower and unite Asian student athletes by creating a supportive and inclusive network that promotes development of community and service through athletic, academic, and cultural lenses.

name: Asian Students Association
description: To create an open space centered in care, a culture of intentional relationship-building, and inclusivity for Duke's Asian community. To form sustainable relationships, support, and be in solidarity with other campus affinity groups. To demand that Duke implement institutional change that creates an inclusive space for marginalized students. To be a communal learning space that is invested in the history of the Asian American as a political identity. To remain accountable and open to the general body's needs and interests, constantly growing and changing as an organization.

name: Asian Theology Group
description: ATG seeks to recognize the unique ways in which Asians and Asian-Americans encounter Christianity and to provide a space for them to share those experiences. In this way, ATG hopes both to help facilitate a support system for Asians and Asian-Americans in the Divinity School as well as to raise awareness of Asian/Asian-American culture and experiences among non-Asians.

name: Asian-Pacific American Medical Students Association at Duke
description: The purpose of Duke APAMSA is to explore and resolve the unique challenges, obstacles, and responsibilities specific to Asian and Pacific Islander health students and health professionals and address health needs specific to Asian and Pacific Islander American (APIA) communities through leadership, education, research, and service as further outlined below:

name: Association for Business Oriented Women at Duke
description: The mission of BOW is to empower business oriented female students by promoting education, experience and exchange among interested students and outstanding industry professionals.

name: Association for Women in Mathematics
description: Founded in 2019, the Association for Women in Mathematics (AWM) Duke Student Chapter is a community of Duke undergraduate and graduate students associated with the national AWM organization.

name: Association of Latino Professionals for America
description: The Duke chapter of the Association of Latino Professionals for America (ALPFA) is dedicated to empowering students through professional development, leadership, mentorship, and community. We strive to create an inclusive environment where students of all backgrounds can build meaningful connections, develop career-ready skills, and grow into leaders prepared to make an impact across every sector of the global economy. Through networking, education, advocacy, and service, ALPFA at Duke fosters both personal and professional growth while celebrating the value of bicultural identity and diverse

name: Association of Mixed People at Duke
description: The mission of the Association of Mixed People at Duke is to build a space of community and support for Duke students who identify as mixed. We aim to help students navigate their multicultural identities through social outreach activities and educational campaigns. We intend to offer a community where their identity will not be questioned but welcomed and celebrated. Students of any mixed-race background can have the opportunity to form bonds with others who have shared similar experiences. Although AMP@D's focus is on celebrating those from multicultural backgrounds, we are open to anyone in

name: Azerbaijani Union at Duke
description: DAU shall be committed to its founding mission to foster cultural exchange, promote understanding of Azerbaijan's heritage, and support the academic and personal growth of Azerbaijani students at Duke University. DAU aims to provide a platform for exchanging cultural values, insights, and perspectives and strengthening ties between Azerbaijani and other cultures while offering a supportive network for its members through events, discussions, and collaborations.

name: Azurebot at Duke
description: Our goal is to provide undergraduate and graduate students with more hands-on opportunities to interact with various technologies and apply their knowledge in building a fleet of robots to compete in one of the most exciting robotics competitions in the world, RoboMaster. With this unique experience, we hope to further students' understanding of mechanical engineering, electrical engineering, computer vision, computer engineering, and embedded control systems to become the true robomaster!

name: Bahá'í Community
description: The Duke Baha'i Community promotes a pattern of campus life where spiritual conversation and service to others go hand-in-hand. Our community building activities aim to foster inner transformation and cultivate a sense of collective ownership for the spiritual, social and economic well-being of both the Duke campus and the wider Durham, NC area.

name: Baldwin Scholars
description: The Baldwin Scholars program contributes to Duke University's mission "to provide a superior liberal education to undergraduate students, attending not only to their intellectual growth but also to their development as adults committed to high ethical standards and full participation as leaders in their communities..." The Program inspires and supports female-identified undergraduate students to become engaged, confident and connected leaders in the Duke community and beyond.

name: Ballet & Books at Duke University
description: Ballet & Books is a national, non-profit organization striving to reduce the literacy gap through the hybrid storytelling of dance and reading. In our free extracurricular programming led by college students, we provide 6-9-year-olds with an opportunity to improve their literacy skills through a combination of dance instruction and dialogic reading. The chapter at Duke University aims to provide this programming for children in the Durham community.

name: Bass Connections
description: Bass Connections bridges the classroom and the real world, giving students a chance to roll up their sleeves and tackle complex societal problems alongside faculty from across Duke. Working in interdisciplinary teams, graduate and undergraduate students collaborate with faculty on cutting-edge research that spans subjects, demographic groups and borders. Bass Connections builds on Duke's culture of collaboration and fosters knowledge in service to society.

name: Bench and Bar Pre-Law Society
description: The mission of Bench and Bar is to provide services to undergraduates interested in pursuing a legal career. Bench and Bar seeks to accomplish its stated goal by acting as an intermediary between undergraduates and the pre-law advising office, providing students with resources for law school admissions, and by fostering interest in the legal field.

name: Beyond Borders
description: Duke Beyond Borders is a student-led club that advocates for justice for (im)migrants, refugees, and asylum seekers in the United States of America.

name: Big Brothers Big Sisters at Duke
description: The mission of BBBS is to create meaningful one-to-one relationships between Bigs (Duke students) and Littles (children from local elementary schools), allowing the former to serve as role models and a loving older siblings to inspire the latter to reach their full potentials. BBBS at Duke works with the local BBBS of the Triangle to accomplish such a mission through training sessions, monthly personal check-ups, as well as seasonal parties that brings Bigs and Littles together on campus to further develop their relationships.

name: Biology Cultural Association
description: The Biology Cultural Association is an organization that seeks to build a community of underrepresented students within the Department of Biology. Vulnerable identities like POC, people with disabilities, religious minorities, low-income students, and sexual and gender minorities, are underrepresented on campus and in STEM. BCA supports undecided underclassmen through 1:1 mentorship between upperclassmen and underclassmen, seminars and panels, academic advising, and social events. We are a safe space for students to voice their unique concerns about representation and diversity initiatives in

name: Biomedical Engineering Ph.D. Student Association
description: The mission of BEPSA is to give a voice to the BME PhD student body and improve the PhD student experience within the BME Department. The organization will facilitate communication between students and faculty, connect students to resources available within the department, and advocate for the department within and outside of the university.

name: Biomedical Engineering Society
description: The Mission of the BMES is to build and support the biomedical engineering community, locally, nationally and internationally, with activities designed to communicate recent advances, discoveries, and inventions; promote education and professional development; and integrate the perspectives of the academic, medical, governmental, and business sectors.

name: Biomedical Graduate Student Council at Duke
Black Arts Collective
description: The mission of Black Arts Collective is: 1. To provide space and resources to platform the work of Black artists at Duke University. 2. To provide foundational artistic workshops and learning opportunities to Black students at Duke University. 3. To facilitate artistic collaborations between Black people across the diaspora.

name: Black Graduate and Professional Students Association
Black in Business
description: The mission of the Black in Business is to promote diversity and cultural enrichment at Duke University; to assist in the development of local Black businesses, and to assist in the recruitment and retention of minorities. We believe the best way to do this is through integrative programming such as talks with alumni, networking mixers with other organizations, and mentoring across schools.

name: Black Policy Student Association
description: The Black Policy Student Association (BPSA) focuses on advancing the interests of Black students and effectuating change in the policy community. Through community engagement, professional development, and advocacy opportunities, BPSA helps educate the Sanford community about the implications of policy involving Black communities while providing spaces for students to engage in meaningful community building. Outside of Sanford, BPSA aims to develop meaningful connections between students and the historically Black Durham community. BPSA hopes to further student engagement within Durham through

name: Black Pre-Law Society at Duke
description: The Black Pre-Law Society (BPLS) at Duke seeks to diversify the legal profession by promoting transparency and accessibility to resources regarding the law school admissions process and legal profession for Black-identifying undergraduate students. BPLS is dedicated to fostering a community of Black excellence, success, networking and mentorship. With these values, we strive to aid Black students in their legal journey.

name: Black Seminarians Union
description: Fellowship: To engender Christian fellowship between Black seminarians, the larger Divinity School, the University and the Durham community. Education: To ensure the development of theological perspectives, commensurate with traditions of the Black Church and further, to educate the larger community regarding Black Church traditions, theology and experiences in America. name: Black Student Alliance
description: We, the members of the Black Student Alliance (BSA) of Duke University, for the sake of the intellectual, social, and cultural enrichment of the Duke community, pledge to cultivate an enlightened, open-minded relationship between the members of the black community in particular and the Duke undergraduate community in general. With this constitution we offer our commitment to the elimination of social barriers on our campus as well as our recognition of the humanity of all people.

name: BlackGen Capital
description: The core mission of BlackGen Capital is to close the access gap by creating a pipeline for talented, underrepresented minority students entering the financial services industry.

name: Blue Crew
description: Empowering varsity women’s sports at Duke by showing up to games, matches, etc. and spreading awareness and excitement for those teams. Additionally this club will be an opportunity for women to grow and learn about professions in the sports space.

name: Blue Devil Bakers
description: At Blue Devil Bakers, our mission is to cultivate a deep appreciation and understanding of the art and science of baking. We are dedicated to exploring and sharing the rich cultural heritage embodied in baking traditions from around the world. Through hands-on workshops, educational sessions, and community events, we aim to enlighten our members about the intricate science behind baking techniques and ingredients. Our goal is to create a welcoming community where enthusiasts and beginners alike can discover the joy and knowledge that baking brings, fostering both skill development and cultural

name: Blue Devil Barbells
description: The mission of our student organization is to provide Duke students with an environment conducive to improving their physical well-being, mental strength and learning proper powerlifting technique. Rather than emphasizing physical traits, powerlifting develops a healthier relationship with food and exercise where athletes are encouraged to build strength, muscle and feel powerful. Everyone is welcome!

name: Blue Devil Birders
description: The mission of Duke Birding Club is to connect students with nature, fostering an appreciation for avian life around campus and Durham. The DBC will focus on local conservation initiatives and changing behavior to promote a bird-friendly campus and community. The DBC will offer birding excursions, professional guest lectures, research and citizen science opportunities. We will provide a welcoming community that is beginner-friendly and open to all. We believe that birding is for everyone, regardless of background, and will grow an inclusive community.

name: Blue Devil Cricket
description: Blue Devil Cricket has two main goals: (1) create a community for people interested in learning, watching, and/or playing cricket; and (2) promote the growth of American cricket by introducing the sport to other students.

name: Blue Devil Gaming
description: The purpose is to be a multi-game gaming organization fostering both the casual and competitive gamers at Duke University. Our focus is to develop a gaming community on campus as well as promote gamers to compete in esports (or "eSports") gaming tournaments with their respective game(s). The goal is to represent the university in a new realm of sports that has been waiting for several years to come.

name: Blue Devils Mental Health First Aid
description: Mental Health First Aid is a course that teaches you how to help someone who is developing a mental health problem or experiencing a mental health crisis. The training helps you identify, understand, and respond to signs of addictions and mental illnesses.

name: Blue Devils United
description: As Blue Devils United (BDU), we value queer and trans communities and strive to empower LGBTQIA+ student voices. We believe in constant learning and growth to promote intersectionality and inclusion. We facilitate coalition-building throughout marginalized communities. We celebrate unapologetic joy.

name: Blue Devils Versus Cancer
description: The purpose of this organization is to support the Duke Cancer Institute (DCI) in their effort to fundraise for cancer research, help improve patient care and accelerate the translation of cancer-related discoveries in the lab into better treatment for cancer patients.

name: Body Empowerment Project
description: The Duke Body Empowerment Project aims to create a safe space for open conversations about body image and mental health, with the goal of dismantling diet culture in all its forms on Duke's campus and beyond. Not only do we aim to provide a tight-knit community for individuals to share their struggles with food, exercise, and/or self-esteem, we also intend to reach the greater Duke community through our online platform and campus-wide advocacy events.

name: BOOST Beyond
description: BOOST Beyond is an extension program of BOOST (Building Opportunities and Overtures in Science and Technology), a multidimensional pathway program to excite students in the Durham Public School system about science. BOOST Beyond serves to expand post-secondary access through individualized mentoring. name: Brain Injury Awareness Club
description: The mission of BrainIAC is to foster a multi-disciplinary community of students who will come together to learn, discuss, engage in community outreach, and spread data-based awareness involving brain injuries. BrainIAC members will engage with researchers, patients, caretakers, and doctors in critical discussions, share stories of people impacted by brain injuries, and connect with the broader Durham community in outreach efforts. name: Bridge and Mathematics Association at Duke
description: BaMA is dedicated to spreading the culture of the card game of bridge, a both social and intellectual game, through combining community-building and algorithmic thinking training. As a game that is slowly being lost in time, this organization is also aimed at preserving and teaching this aged game. In addition, BaMA strives to connecting Duke students with bridge players in Durham and the surrounding area.

name: Bridging Resources for Interdisciplinary Innovation, Discovery, Growth, and Exploration
description: This group is dedicated to fostering meaningful connections across academic disciplines to enhance the personal and professional growth of graduate and professional students at Duke. We believe that creativity and innovation flourish when diverse perspectives intersect, yet graduate students across fields remain isolated from one another and are often unaware of opportunities to collaborate outside their home department. name: Brighter Smile Foundation
description: The Brighter Smile Foundation at Duke is dedicated to improving oral health and promoting brighter, healthier smiles within the Durham community. Our chapter focuses on addressing gaps in access to preventive oral care by providing essential dental hygiene products and education to underserved populations in the local area. As Duke students and volunteers in the Durham community, we recognize that there is often a disconnect between the university and the populations we aim to serve. Our organization is intentional about bridging this gap by working closely with local volunteers, community org

name: Bring Happiness for Hospice
description: In order to ease the process of dying for both the patient and the family, hospice is an essential component of end-of-life care. Patients are given comfort and medical care during their last days alive, and families are given greater peace and ease while losing their loved one. However, due to the high cost of hospice care, families often lack the means to fulfill their loved one's wishes while paying for the care itself. name: Bringing Hope to the Family Duke
description: Bringing Hope to the Family is dedicated to supporting the education of children in the rural village of Kaihura, Uganda by organizing fundraising events and supply drives. We believe that education is the key to unlocking potential and breaking the cycle of poverty.

name: Broader Blue Devils
description: The mission of Broader Blue Devils is to cultivate a deeper understanding and appreciation of diverse cultures among Duke undergraduate students. Food is a powerful medium for cultural exchange, offering insights into the traditions, values, and histories that shape various communities. Through hands-on exploration of cultural cuisine and regional specialties, BBD aims to create an immersive experience that goes beyond taste.

name: Buddhist Meditation Community at Duke
description: BMCD provides Duke students from various spiritual backgrounds with the opportunity to learn about Buddhist teachings and practice meditation. Our Monday evening meetings include quiet meditation, group study and discussion.

name: Bull City Scholars
description: Our mission, as Bull City Scholars, is to create a sustainable mentorship and tutoring program centered around educational equity and college access for middle school students in Durham that are actively underserved by Duke's Partnerships for Service. To support an informed framework of service, students may participate in an optional, introductory house course investigating education inequality and pedagogy.

name: Business Behind Health at Duke
description: Business Behind Health at Duke invites students of all backgrounds to explore untapped careers in the health and wellness economy. Considering many Duke students feel a disconnect between their academic interests and career options beyond clinical roles, DBBH is Duke's first student organization dedicated to offering a centralized network integrating business, technology and healthcare perspectives. By showcasing non-traditional roles and being an engine for cross-sector collaboration, DBBH is committed to helping each student find their place in the health industry.

name: Business of Entertainment, Arts and Media
description: A student-run organization committed to empowering students with tactical skills, industry connections, and professional opportunities needed to launch successful business careers in entertainment, arts, and media.

name: Business of Retail Society at Duke
description: Retail and Consumer Goods sectors are vastly underrepresented in Duke's pre-professional scene. Hundreds of students across campus have expressed interest in fashion, beauty, PR, marketing, editorial, creative branding, and entrepreneurship with no outlet to put their skills and passions into practice. Through robust programming, including speaker events, career talks, skill-building workshops, and intimate networking sessions, DBRS aims to empower members while cultivating a community of like-minded individuals.

name: Camp Kesem at Duke University
description: Camp Kesem is a weeklong, sleep-away camp for children aged 6-18 who are affected by a parent or caregiver's cancer. It is free for the campers and is designed to provide a week of support, community, and fun for Camp Kesem campers. In addition to camp, we offer support to families throughout the year in the form of birthday cards, virtual cabin chat meetings, one in-person event for camper families each semester, and connection to resources. name: Cards for Humanity
description: 1. Cards for Humanity aims to host and teach diverse card games from around the world to connect and engage Duke’s diverse student body with one another and with members of the Durham community, allowing students to participate in games they already played or learn new ones while getting to know each other and become better acquainted with Durham. 2. Cards for Humanity aims to organize interactive events at local community centers ranging from nursing homes and senior centers to hospitals/clinics and high schools, using card games as a medium to engage and connect with members, including those

name: CARE Connections
description: CARE Connections aims to serve as a reliable resource that addresses social isolation and social drivers of health for older adults in the community, a historically marginalized population. We provide weekly well-check calls, free health fairs, urgent food delivery, and resource connection to local resources related to food insecurity, transportation, and housing. The weekly well-check calls are the foundation of the program: volunteers are paired with senior partners with the goal of establishing authentic and trusting relationships. name: Career Center
description: Our mission is to serve the Duke Community as the comprehensive career center committed to the education and development of the whole person, integrating academic, personal and career development.

name: Cartoonists' Collective at Duke
description: The mission of the Cartoonists’ Collective at Duke (CCD) is to provide a community for Duke students who appreciate or are interested in creating comics, cartoons, and related art forms. Moreover, we strive to promote these art forms on campus and beyond through publications and creative collaborations with other organizations. CCD aims to be a diverse community that embraces creators regardless of style, medium, or genre of interest. We welcome prospective members of all skill levels, from beginners to experienced artists and creators. There are many dimensions to making comics and cartoons,

name: Catalyst
description: The mission of Catalyst is to build a social and pre-professional community of tech-enthusiasts. Catalyst aims to accomplish three goals: 1) To allow students to obtain mentorship in the field of technology. 2) To allow students to be connected with peers with similar interests. 3) To inspire each other to research and learn more about opportunities and disciplines within technology. This organization is also intended to provide a new insight into what comprises the field of technology. Catalyst members will meet biweekly for a General Body Meeting.

name: Center for Jewish Studies
description: The Jewish Studies Program at Duke University originated in the 1940s and was formally established in 1972. Today, the Center for Jewish Studies is an inter-departmental program that sponsors a wide variety of cultural events, offers educational programs, and fosters academic research and scholarly exchange of ideas. The Center for Jewish Studies is committed to interdisciplinary engagement in a global academic community. In addition to our internationally respected faculty, Duke is home to one of the finest collections of Jewish haggadot, theological and liturgical printed works, manuscripts,

name: Center for Multicultural Affairs
description: The Center for Multicultural Affairs is where students find themselves and their community through curiosity and collaboration with care.

name: Center for Muslim Life
description: The Center for Muslim Life (CML) supports students in bridging their faith and values with their Duke experience. We foster an environment where Muslim students can thrive, while enriching campus understanding of Islam through meaningful engagement with students, faculty, staff, and alumni of all backgrounds.

name: Center for Sexual and Gender Diversity
description: We strive to achieve an inclusive campus climate for students, staff, faculty, and alumnx with marginalized sexual orientations, gender identities, and gender expressions through education, advocacy, support, mentoring, academic engagement, and providing space.

name: Chabad Graduate Student Group
description: The primary purpose of the Lubavitch/Chabad Student Group is to provide living Judaism to the students at Duke within the framework of traditional Judaism. Our objectives include but are not limited to: educational, ritual, and social activities, in addition to counseling and spiritual guidance to individual students. Our organization is based on Chassidic philosophy, as taught locally by the Lubavitch/Chabad Jewish Center directed by Rabbi Zalman & Yehudis Bluming. name: Chabad Student Group
description: The primary purpose of the Chabad Student Group is to provide vibrant Jewish life to the Jewish students at the Duke University within the framework of traditional Judaism. Our objectives include but are not limited to: educational, ritual, and social activities, in addition to counseling and spiritual guidance to individual students. Our organization is based on Chassidic philosophy, as taught locally by Chabad at Duke directors Rabbi Nossen & Chaya Fellig. Our philosophy states that every Jew deserves an equal opportunity to experience and enjoy their heritage. All programs and events of the

name: Challah for Hunger at Duke (a project of Nazun)

name: National Society of Black Engineers
description: The mission of the National Society of Black Engineers is "to increase the number of culturally responsible Black Engineers who excel academically, succeed professionally, and positively impact the community."

name: Native American Graduate and Professional Student Association
description: Our mission is to foster a visible community of Native graduate/professional students as well as faculty and allies at Duke. We will provide a space for social and cultural activities, facilitate interdisciplinary scholarship and professional development, represent the concerns and goals of Native students at an institutional level, mentor and collaborate with Duke's Native undergraduates, participate in interinstitutional events, and build reciprocal relationships with off-campus Native communities. name: Native American/Indigenous Student Alliance
description: As the primary Native American/Indigenous cultural organization on campus, we serve as a resource for all Native American/Indigenous students on campus through educational, career, cultural, and social support. Further, we work to advance the awareness of Native American/Indigenous cultures across campus, throughout the state of North Carolina, and beyond.

name: NeuroCare
description: The mission of NeuroCare is to raise awareness by educating Duke students about neurological and psychiatric disorders and their prevention, advocate for research for cure, and help build a support system for those suffering from these disorders.

name: Neuroscience Majors' Union
description: The Neuroscience Majors' Union serves to promote a sense of community among undergraduate Neuroscience majors, to encourage student involvement with the Duke Undergraduate Studies in Neuroscience program and to support interdisciplinary collaboration through the participation of interested parties across campus.

name: New Creation Arts
description: New Creation Arts exists to foster creative, theological, and liturgical engagement with the arts at Duke Divinity School and the surrounding and global community. It does this through regular art exhibits in the Divinity School, including an annual, themed Juried Arts Exhibit; fellowship activities, and lending support to other groups hosting arts-related events.

name: New Neighbors Project
description: The New Neighbors Project aims to forge meaningful connections between local newcomer families—refugees, immigrants, and others—and the Duke community. Through the program, each Duke student is paired with a newcomer child to cultivate strong relationships and promote college readiness through personalized, one-on-one weekly sessions.

name: Nic School Divers
description: We are a collective of students at The Nicholas School of the Environment at Duke University who are committed to the practice of Citizen Science and Ocean and Marine Conservation through SCUBA diving.

name: Nicholas Net Impact Club
description: The mission of the Nicholas School Net Impact Chapter is to inspire, educate, and equip individuals to use the power of business to create a more socially and environmentally sustainable world. To fulfill this mission, Nicholas School Net Impact Chapter will remain committed to providing its members with an array of opportunities that will: 1) Develop and strengthen the skills, instincts, abilities, and resources of environmental management students to become leaders in the sustainability field and influence change. 2) Grow the professional network of Nicholas School of the Environment student

name: Nicholas School Energy Club
description: The Nicholas School Energy Club is a student-led organization that strives to unite students, alumni, professionals, and community members over current and emerging energy trends. Through networking events, speaker series, career treks, and workshops, club members will have the opportunity to learn and get connected to Duke’s many resources to develop the knowledge and skills needed to lead the energy transition.

name: Nicholas School Golf Club
description: The Nic School Golf club aims to provide instructional, social, and environmental learning opportunities for golfers of all skill levels.

name: Nicholas School Naturalists
description: Our mission is to foster community-building, leadership development, and place-based environmental education for Nicholas School graduate students. Facilitated by students for students, our activities include naturalist walks, day trips, camping and backpacking trips, and other guided excursions. We aim to help connect students in the Nicholas School to each other and to the landscapes of the Triangle, North Carolina, and the greater Southeast.

name: Nicholas School Partners and Spouses
description: This group intends to make students and their partners feel welcome at the Nicholas School and the Duke community, and soften the transition process to Durham through social networking.

name: Nicholas School Student Council
description: The Nicholas School Student Council (NSSC) of the Nicholas School of the Environment is an advocate on behalf of professional students, representing the interests and concerns of these students to the Duke University and Nicholas School community. The NSSC is a group of elected Masters of Environmental Management (MEM) and Masters of Forestry (MF) students that serves as an advisory body to the faculty and administration, and provides a conduit between the student body, faculty, and administration. Through the NSSC, professional students address with faculty and administration issues that incl

name: Nurse Anesthesia Program SRNA Association
description: A. To assume responsibility for contributing to nurse anesthesia education at DUSON in order to provide for the highest quality of healthcare. B. To provide DUSON an understanding of the DUNAP program's fundamental interests and concerns to nurse anesthesiology. C. To aid in the development of the whole person, their professional role, their responsibility for healthcare of people from all settings.

name: Ocean Policy Working Group
description: The OPWG aims to facilitate cross disciplinary discussions and collaborations that explore the political, economic, scientific, and cultural dimensions of human interactions with the ocean. Our activities examine current issues involving the global oceans and the impact of these issues on marine policy and ocean governance. We strive to relate to an audience beyond those that directly study the coast. The OPWG seeks to accomplish its stated goals by hosting seminars, an annual symposium, producing an online publication, film screenings, and other opportunities for its members to gather and dis

name: Oceans@Duke
description: To connect students from various graduate degree programs who have an interest in ocean innovations and solutions. Together, students will work towards building and planning a Blue Economy Summit (online or in-person) with the focus of connecting students to important stakeholders and organizations doing work in ocean sustainability across private and public sectors.

name: Office of University Scholars and Fellows
description: The Office of University Scholars and Fellows, OUSF, supports students through participation in an intellectual community of peers, faculty, alumni, and staff that engage in scholarly and civic endeavors, preparing them to address the most pressing challenges of a changing world.

name: Omega Psi Phi Fraternity, Inc.
description: Omega Psi Phi Fraternity, Inc. was the first historically Black Greek-letter society to be founded on the campus of a Historically Black College/University (HBCU) on November 17th, 1911. The Winning Omega Zeta chapter was the first Black Greek letter organization chartered at Duke on Friday, April 12th 1974. The Omega Zeta chapter serves the community through mentorship, various programs, and service projects centered around the 4 Cardinal Principles of Manhood, Scholarship, Perseverance, and Uplift.

name: On Tap
description: The mission of On Tap is to explore and showcase the art of tap dance at Duke University. On Tap seeks to provide its members with the opportunity to improve their technique through regular rehearsals and performances of original choreography.

name: One for All
description: One For All's purpose is to promote spiritual inclusivity and dialogue to educate and inspire college students towards peace and purity by creating an environment of meaningful discussion about God, Guidance, and Goodness through preparing members to contribute to a global, diverse community from the teachings of the Qur’an and through the example of Prophet Muhammad.

name: oSTEM at Duke University
description: oSTEM is an LGBTQ+ affinity group for graduate students at Duke who are interested in supporting the queer student body! We host regular social and outreach events to build our community and connect students from different STEM departments, as well as offer professional networking opportunities and connections to the local Durham LGBTQ+ network.

name: OUE Faculty Fellows
description: Faculty Fellows serve as a catalyst for intellectual engagement within an assigned West Campus Quad, providing opportunities for students to explore personal and academic topics with a faculty member over a meal along with a small group of students. Faculty Fellows are dynamic scholars and teachers with a passion for integrating the Duke academic experience with students' social and residential lives.

name: Our Urban Future
description: Our Urban Future is Duke University’s undergraduate urban studies club. We are a venue for academic engagement, pre-professional development, and activism promoting sustainable and equitable urbanism. Our core values of inclusion, community, social justice, and learning guide our events and programming both on and off campus.

name: Out of the Blue
description: The mission of Out of the Blue is to share our love of music with each other and our audiences. We strive to create beautiful music using voice and vocal percussion to bring life into well-crafted arrangements and closely knit harmonies. We aim to further our knowledge of and appreciation for music through collaboration.

name: Outing Club
description: The Duke Outing Club seeks to provide authentic opportunities for student-led outdoor recreation. At its core, the organization promotes activities that relate to wilderness travel, exploration, and adventure. By doing so, we believe our actions facilitate appreciation for the natural world and equitable access to all outdoor spaces.

name: Pakistani Students Association
description: The mission of PSA is "to provide a platform for Pakistani and non-Pakistani students alike to connect with the country's rich culture, engage with the issues facing it, and form a network of support and community for all those who associate with it. PSA seeks to accomplish this mission by having several events, such as a speaker series (where we would like to invite prominent people connected with Pakistani culture to speak on campus), cricket games, board game nights, etc."

name: Pancakes for Parkinson's
description: The mission of Pancakes for Parkinson's is to spread awareness about Parkinson's disease and to raise money to support The Michael J. Fox Foundation for Parkinson's Research. The goal of The Michael J. Fox Foundation is to find a cure for Parkinson's disease. P4P seeks to accomplish this mission by hosting a fundraising event each spring on the quad.

name: Partners In Health Engage
description: The mission of PIH Engage is to support the global health nonprofit Partners in Health as part of a national network and grassroots organization. PIH Engage seeks to accomplish this mission through fundraising, advocacy for global health policy/funding, and education of various health concerns around the world.

name: Pediatric Association at Duke
description: The mission of the Duke Pediatric Association is to educate undergraduate students about pediatric health and medicine, foster meaningful dialogue around child health and public health equity, and build a supportive community of future healthcare professionals committed to improving the well-being of children and families. Through educational programming, speaker events, service initiatives, and research and clinical exposure, Duke Pediatric Association seeks to inspire students to pursue compassionate, community-centered pediatric care.

name: Peer Advocacy for Sexual Health
description: The mission of Peer Advocacy for Sexual Health (PASH) is to provide Duke students with sexual health resources and education. This includes: providing students with safer sex supplies after major distribution centers on campus have closed, fostering open conversations on sexual pleasure as an integral part of sexual health, connecting students with trained faculty and staff on campus that specialize in various aspects of sexual health, providing a half-credit sexual health course, and encouraging peer-to-peer discourse on sexual health among the Duke student community.

name: Persian Students Association at Duke University
description: To serve as a tangible presence on campus for the purposes of: facilitating the education of Persian culture and identity on Duke’s campus through cultural learning opportunities; providing support systems for all Duke Persian students; raising awareness about contemporary issues facing Persian students and people of Persian identities; creating spaces to engage in political, social, and cultural debates surrounding issues affecting people of Persian heritage.

name: Phi Alpha Delta
description: Phi Alpha Delta is the premier international law fraternity, and it promotes the highest standard of ethics and professionalism within law schools and the legal profession. Duke's chapter seeks to create a supportive and collaborative community of pre-law students.

name: Phi Beta Sigma Fraternity, Inc.
description: The mission of our chapter is to utilize the skills of our brothers to foster positive change in Durham, enriching fellowship with one another, and cultivating meaningful relationships within our community.

name: Phi Delta Epsilon International Medical Fraternity
description: Phi Delta Epsilon Medical Fraternity creates physicians of integrity with a lifelong commitment to our guiding principles.

name: Planned Parenthood Generation Action Duke
description: PPGA at Duke advances sexual health education on campus, supports local Planned Parenthood health centers, and mobilizes students to speak out for reproductive rights globally.

name: Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery Interest Group
description: A medical student group created to provide additional resources to students interested in plastic and reconstructive surgery. Through research mixers and lecture series we aim to introduce students to our incredible faculty and highlight the frontiers of both basic and clinical research within the division of Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery at Duke.

name: Policy for the People
description: Policy for the People is an organization built around promoting equity, activism, and systems-level change within Duke and local communities. Our mission is to facilitate a deeper understanding of the policy process by translating curriculum into action. We do this through partnership with change-makers and harnessing the power of Sanford students who are interested in creating systems-level change. We host educational events and skills-based workshops, support local policy-change campaigns, and promote community-building programming to support action-oriented change.

name: Policy in Living Color
description: Policy in Living Color (PiLC) is a Sanford-based student organization dedicated to advancing the interests of communities of color. Through informal social gatherings, formal educational workshops, and advocacy opportunities, PiLC provides education to the Sanford community and spaces for students to engage in meaningful discussion. Outside of Sanford, PiLC aims to connect with Durham community members and to continuously uplift their interests through advocacy, policy, and organizing. name: Policy Society at Duke
description: Our mission at DPS is to help students turn their interests in policy into actionable ambitions, pre-professional opportunities, and ultimately, careers that excite them.

name: Population Health Sciences Graduate Student Association
description: The Population Health Sciences Graduate Student Association fosters interdisciplinary collaboration and engages students in initiatives that inspire excellence in service, diversity, and community. We represent the interests, needs, and welfare of our student body to drive positive change and uphold Duke's tradition of leadership and innovation in population health sciences. name: Pratt Energy and Sustainability Club
description: To promote awareness of energy and sustainability focused career paths amongst engineering master's/PhD students. To accomplish this goal, we provide the professional development, knowledge-sharing, and networking needed for impactful careers in the rapidly evolving landscape of sustainability, clean energy and climate change solutions. In the face of the growing interest in climate tech, we aim to explore diverse engineering opportunities within this field and collectively contribute to a meaningful and positive impact on our planet.

name: Pratt Peers Student Support Network
description: The Pratt Peers Student Support Network (Pratt Peers) is a student-led initiative committed to fostering a culture of care, connection, and well-being among engineering graduate students. As trained peer listeners and mentors, Pratt Peers empower students to navigate the academic, social, and emotional aspects of graduate life with confidence and resilience. name: Pre-health Latinx Undergraduate Society
description: The purpose of the PLUS chapter at Duke is to support Duke undergraduate Latino/a/x students on the pre-health track through social, cultural, and educational activities, and is open to all interested in supporting this growth.

name: Primary Care Student Alliance
description: The Primary Care Student Alliance (PCSA) is an interdisciplinary student organization that aims to broaden students' perspectives on what is encompassed by primary care. Going beyond clinical practice, our programming is based on four pillars: Advocacy, Education & Research, Mentorship, and Community Engagement.

name: Prison Justice Action Committee
description: PJAC exists to increase education and offer volunteer opportunities that intersect the carceral system in an interdisciplinary manner, doing both in partnership with the local Durham community. PJAC seeks to bridge the theological education of seminary with the reality of those who are affected by incarceration. name: Product@Duke
description: Product@Duke’s mission is to foster a close-knit community of students dedicated to becoming future leaders in product management. We are committed to helping students develop and apply skills in product management, marketing, and design. By partnering with a diverse range of companies, from local startups to major corporations, our club provides valuable, pro-bono services to assist in product development.

name: Program II Majors Union
description: Enhance the experience of current and prospective Program II students through meaningful mentorship, community-building events, and useful programming.

name: Progress. Period.
description: Progress Period strives to eradicate period poverty and stigma through service, education, and advocacy. Through the distribution of menstrual products and championing of menstrual equity in policy, we aim to center those disproportionately affected by period poverty and support local efforts for menstrual equity.

description: The mission of Project HEAL is to implement and conduct service projects in Latin America and Durham with the goal of reducing global health disparities, particularly those of child and maternal health, through education and empowerment. We value sustainable development and preventative measures that aim to improve community health and help bridge the gap between Duke and Durham. description: Started in 2018, Pureun is a Kpop-focused dance group at Duke. Pureun aims to create an avenue for those interested in Kpop and represent Korean pop-culture to the Duke and North Carolina community. We cover dances to all music genres within the South Korean music industry, including R&B, pop, ballad, and more. As a culture group, we strive to include people from all cultural and social backgrounds and celebrate our love for music and dance.

name: Quantitative Finance and Analytics Club at Duke
description: The Quantitative Finance and Analytics Club at Duke is a student-led organization dedicated to equipping quantitatively driven professional students with the tools, insights, and connections to excel in modern finance. We explore the intersection of data science, machine learning, and quantitative methods in diverse financial applications, including risk modeling, asset management, insurance solutions, portfolio management, game theory, and alternative investments. name: Quantum Information Society at Duke
description: Our mission is to grow the quantum community by promoting the accessibility of quantum information science, quantum computing, and related fields to more Duke students.

description: QuestBridge (QB) is a nationally renowned scholarship organization with 40 chapters at many of the nation's most prestigious universities (i.e. Stanford University, University of Pennsylvania, MIT, Princeton, Columbia University etc.). Duke began accepting QuestBridge students in 2017 and is accepting more than 30 QuestBridge students every year. The Duke QuestBridge Chapter aspires to create a welcoming community for any QuestBridge scholars at Duke and its advocates. Red Cross at Duke
description: The American Red Cross prevents and alleviates human suffering in the face of emergencies by mobilizing the power of volunteers and the generosity of donors. Specifically, our club strives to aid our community by donating and helping acquire blood donations to help those in need.

name: Reformed University Fellowship

name: Research Scholars Program at Duke
description: The mission of RSPr is to establish and facilitate a structured program that introduces underclassmen to research opportunities at Duke, a widely recognized, pre-eminent international research institution, and to fuel members' passion throughout their undergraduate careers. DRSPr seeks to integrate the most critical components of a positive and meaningful research experience with a process that allows motivated students to connect with dedicated research mentors. name: Resource Ambassadors for Coordinating Campus Operations and Organizing Nutrition Solutions at Duke
description: The RACCOONS group is comprised of student volunteers overseen by faculty to reduce food waste on campus. The club members, also known as resource ambassadors, will coordinate food removal and disposal from campus operations and events, ensuring good quality excess food is repurposed rather than discarded. Our efforts are closely aligned with Duke's broader climate initiatives to reduce waste and support sustainability. RACCOONS will create a sustainable, efficient system that provides nutritious solutions to food insecurity, whilst simultaneously reducing the food waste problem on campus.

name: Revive Book Club
description: This club’s goal is to create a community of readers on campus who engage in thought provoking conversations and develop a deeper appreciation for the contribution of black authors. The objective is to enlighten students on the culture of this sub-sector of literature that they may not have been exposed to in the past.

name: Rhythm & Blue
description: The mission of Rhythm & Blue is to bring friends together to make beautiful a cappella music.

name: Robotics
description: The Duke Robotics Club is a student-run organization in Duke University's Pratt School of Engineering. Our mission is to provide Duke undergraduate and graduate students a place to pursue their interest in robotics by working on high-impact, large-scale robotics projects and competitions, primarily in the realm of Autonomous Underwater Vehicles (AUVs). These projects allow our talented students to hone their skills and demonstrate the strength of Duke Engineering.

name: Robotics and Diving Club
description: The goal of the Robotics and Diving club (RAD) is to provide Duke students and faculty the opportunity to pursue scuba diving as an interdisciplinary method to explore environmental passions and engineering.

name: Root Causes Undergraduate Coalition
description: The mission of Duke RCUC is to assist in the operations of Root Causes, a community organization based in the Duke University School of Medicine that is focused on alleviating disparities caused by the social determinants of health in the greater Durham area. Specifically, members will have the opportunity to work with the various components of Root Causes addressing different social determinants of health, including, but not limited to, the Fresh Produce Program, Healthy STEPS, Project FEED, and WellNest. description: The mission of Rotaract is to provide an opportunity for young adults to enhance the knowledge and skills that will assist them in personal development, to address the physical and social needs of their communities, and to promote better relations between all people worldwide through a framework of friendship and service.

name: Run 4 Raj at Duke
description: The mission of Run 4 Raj at Duke is to celebrate and honor the life of Raj Mehta, a beloved member of the Duke community, who tragically passed away on March 27th, 2020. Raj, a member of the Class of 2023, touched the lives of many as a student, friend, and family member, making lasting impacts through his kind demeanor and involvement with organizations such as Camp Kesem and Duke Dhamaka. Run 4 Raj unites these groups—along with others—to keep his memory alive. name: Runway of Dreams at Duke
description: Runway of Dreams at Duke will provide an interdisciplinary space to empower people with disabilities on the runway and to advance the future of adaptive design and innovation through a variety of design workshops, semester-long projects, fundraising events, and runway shows.

name: Sabrosura
description: Duke University’s premier Latin dance team, Sabrosura is a co-ed, student-run, student-choreographed, and student-developed dance group. We specialize in salsa, merengue, bachata, and reggaeton, among other styles. Sabro is all about having fun as we dance together, building a community, and spreading the best parts of Latin culture through dance.

name: Sanford Education Policy Club
description: The Sanford Education Policy Club (SEP) aims to represent students interested in education policy by fostering a career and community network and amplifying key issues. SEP provides opportunities for students to participate in career development events, join an education policy community, and engage with key stakeholders on policy issues.

name: Sanford Energy and Environment Club
description: The Sanford Energy and Environment Club provides opportunities for future policy leaders from across Duke to engage with environmental policy issues, find community, and connect with their environment. These opportunities include speaker events, workshops, experiential activities, and social gatherings that empower us to engage with diverse and intersectional environmental policy issues including the energy transition, conservation, sustainable development, and environmental justice.

name: Sanford Golf Club
description: The Sanford Golf Club aims to foster the love of the game, one swing at a time, by hosting social events that bring together students with a general interest in golf, connecting novice golfers to instructional resources, and facilitating regular competition.

name: Sanford Latin American and Caribbean Student Group
description: Sanford LAC's mission is to lead and support academic, career, outreach, cultural, and social efforts of the Sanford community focused on Latin America and the Caribbean (LAC) in order to strengthen collaboration and engagement between LAC and Sanford.

name: Sanford Pride
description: PridePol exists to provide space and opportunities for the LGBTQIA+ community at Sanford to come together in coalition and power. The organization aims to amplify and support the efforts of queer individuals, events, and issues on the Duke campus, within the Durham community, and beyond. In addition, PridePol facilitates opportunities for Sanford students to learn about and advance policies affecting the queer community and our intersectional allies.

name: Sanford Run Club
description: The mission of the Sanford Run Club is to promote community and a healthy lifestyle through social runs and walks around campus and the Durham community. Sanford Run Club facilitates a welcoming environment where anyone looking for activity and community can join and destress with friends. Club membership means becoming part of a community that values support, friendship, camaraderie, and fun.

name: Sanford School of Public Policy Student Council
description: The Sanford Student Council supports the endeavors of the Master of Public Policy (MPP) student body, ensures students' needs and goals are heard, and promotes Terry Sanford's legacy of doing the right thing in a difficult moment. The Council brings concerns, questions, and recommendations regarding the MPP program to the administration. The Council facilitates student involvement in Sanford School planning in partnership with the Director of Graduate Studies and MPP Director of Student Services.

name: Sanford Social Committee
description: The Sanford MPP Social Committee is a group that fosters connections and relationships, and adds value to the social life of the Master of Public Policy (MPP) program. The Committee facilitates popularly conceived events that are fun, inclusive, and feasible within the Committee's budget constraints, as well as the time constraints of its volunteer members. Membership on the Committee entails serving as a voice for classmates, generating event ideas, and basic administrative/logistical work associated with hosting events.

name: Sanford Urban Policy Club
description: The Sanford Urban Policy Club (SUP) is a graduate student organization at the Sanford School of Public Policy that helps students explore and discuss the issues facing Durham and other cities across the country. SUP hosts and promotes events for engaging researchers, practitioners, and other students about the best practices, political considerations, and structural constraints presently shaping city-level policy decisions.

name: Sanford Veterans Association
description: Sanford Veterans Association (SVA) fosters a supportive community for active duty, retired, and separated service members at the Sanford School of Public Policy.

name: Sanford Women in Policy
description: Sanford Women in Policy (SWP) is a graduate student organization at the Sanford School of Public Policy that provides a forum to discuss and address challenges and opportunities for women in the field of public policy. SWP also serves as a space to cultivate, empower, and promote unity and fellowship for those who identify as women and their allies. SWP creates opportunities for leadership, professional development, and dialogue for its members. description: Duke's Premier Business Society

description: Our mission is to Foster a community that celebrates Scandinavia's rich heritage and cultural diversity. We will provide a welcoming space for Scandinavian students, creating a sense of home and familiarity in a foreign environment. Simultaneously, we are committed to inclusivity and cultural exchange, inviting all Duke students, regardless of their background, to explore and appreciate Scandinavian traditions, values, and contemporary life. Through social events, cultural workshops, and educational programs, we aim to enhance understanding and appreciation of Scandinavian culture on campus, w

name: Science Olympiad and Science Bowl at Duke
description: The mission of Duke University Science Olympiad is to bridge the Duke-Durham gap by promoting Duke student involvement in Science Olympiad in the local Durham area and nationally in the United States through mentorship. DUSO seeks to accomplish this mission by hosting an elementary Division A tournament every spring, hosting a national middle school Division B and high school Division C invitation every fall or spring, and developing an outreach program for local elementary and middle schools to encourage interest in STEM activities.

name: Secular Student Alliance at Duke
description: SSA at Duke fosters a welcoming community for secular, nonreligious, atheist, agnostic, questioning, ex-religious, and religiously diverse students. The Organization promotes separation of church and state, critical inquiry, evidence-based dialogue, secular values, humanism, ethics, human rights, and freedom of conscience. SSA at Duke is affiliated with the national Secular Student Alliance, providing access to resources, speakers, training, and organizational support.

name: Sexual Harassment and Assault Prevention & Education
description: SHAPE is a student advocacy organization working to eradicate sexual violence through prevention, education, and response efforts at Duke. We want to see the day where Duke doesn't need SHAPE. Until then, SHAPE will be on the frontline igniting cultural and institutional, survivor-centric change.

name: Shave and Buzz at Duke University
description: The purpose of this organization is to support the I'm Not Done Yet Foundation in raising money for AYA cancer research. To do so, the organization will hold an annual shave in the Spring of each semester where the proceeds will go directly towards AYA cancer research and programs which the I'm Not Done Yet Foundation supports (nearly all programs are run in conjunction with the Duke Hospital). The fundraiser will consist of members volunteering to get their heads shaved to promote cancer awareness, as well as soliciting donations in the weeks leading up to the shave. name: Sigma Gamma Rho Sorority, Inc.
description: The purpose of the Omicron Nu Chapter shall be to implement the vision, mission, and programs of Sigma Gamma Rho Sorority, Incorporated in accordance with the governing documents of the sorority at Duke University.

name: Singapore Students Association
description: Duke University Singapore Students Association (Duke SSA) aims to provide a "home away from home" for students who are from Singapore and/or feel an affinity to Singapore. We also strive to raise awareness of the unique Singapore culture at Duke University.

name: Sisters in STEM
description: Sisters in STEM (SIS) is a group that gives Black women in STEM at the graduate level at Duke a place to get together and socialize on a monthly basis throughout the semester. We give members a safe place to express their ideas, support one another, and network with other Black women in STEM across various graduate programs on campus. We are devoted to creating an accepting community where everyone can be seen and heard.

name: Skydiving at Duke
description: The mission of the Duke University Skydiving Club is to foster a safe, inclusive, and supportive community for students interested in skydiving, while promoting personal growth, adventure, and responsible participation in the sport. The purpose of the Duke University Skydiving Club is to introduce students to the sport of skydiving through education, training opportunities, and group experiences. The club aims to prioritize safety, encourage teamwork and leadership, and build a community of thrill-seekers who share a passion for pushing boundaries and embracing new challenges.

name: SNUGS at Duke
description: Our goal is to create a safer world for special needs children by connecting student communities with local families. We want to increase safety for children with intellectual/developmental differences by tackling accidental drowning. Our objective is to ensure that more low-income families have access to quality, one-on-one swim instruction for their children with special needs. To do this, SNUGS creates free swim clinic programs on university campuses across the country.

description: SHPE changes lives by empowering the Hispanic community to realize its fullest potential and to impact the world through STEM awareness, access, support, and development. The purpose of this Chapter is to realize the mission of SHPE at Duke University by organizing events and programs that directly lead members towards their post-graduation success.

name: Society of Physics Students
description: The mission of SPS is to promote physics community and academic opportunity among undergraduates at Duke.

description: Our mission is to inspire and empower both graduate and undergraduate students by fostering a deep understanding of the field of technical sales, also known as presales or solutions consulting. Through strategic collaboration with the National Society of Sales Engineers (NSSE), we aim to provide unique opportunities for learning, professional growth, and industry engagement. name: Society of Women Engineers
description: The mission of the Society of Women Engineers Duke Section is as follows. First, to inform young women, their parents, counselors, and the general public, of the qualifications and achievements of women engineers and the opportunities open to them. Second, to serve as a center of information on women in engineering. Lastly, to encourage women engineers to attain high levels of education and professional achievement.

name: Society-Centered AI
description: The SCAI Student Group empowers Duke students to explore, question, and shape the future of society‑centered AI. Our mission is to build a vibrant, multidisciplinary community that engages with AI’s impact on people, institutions, and the world—through events, discussions, and hands‑on opportunities connected to the Society-Centered AI initiative.

name: Something Borrowed Something Blue
description: To spread the message of God through music and fellowship.

name: South Asian Medical Student Association
description: The mission of the South Asian Medical Student Association is to provide a cultural, social, and advocacy group for medical students who identify as part of the South Asian community.

name: Southeast Asian Community at Duke
description: The mission of Southeast Asian Community at Duke (Duke SEAC) is to - a. SOLIDARITY — Build understanding and solidarity between Southeast Asian Americans and internationals, and across diverse Southeast Asian ethnic communities. b. EDUCATION — Share Southeast Asian cultures, histories, and experiences with the broader Duke community. c. ADVOCACY — Advocate for greater visibility, representation, and Institutional support for Southeast Asian students at Duke. d. COMMUNITY — Build a close-knit and inclusive Southeast Asian student family.

name: Spark
description: Sophomore Spark provides a coordinated approach to supporting second-year students in their efforts to seek purpose, build resilience, and navigate academic and career journeys. Sophomore Spark offers a series of opportunities to come together with peers, faculty, staff, and alumni as they traverse their second year at Duke.

description: The primary mission of Speak of the Devil is to create and perform great all-male a cappella at Duke University and around the Durham community. Speak seeks to accomplish this goal by fostering a productive musical environment at all of their shows, practices, and events.
