description: The mission of Duke Unified Special Olympics is to bring together Duke students and individuals with intellectual disabilities through sports, friendship, advocacy, and inclusive community experiences. Our goal is to create meaningful relationships while promoting inclusion both on campus and throughout the Durham community. Our chapter offers two Unified intramural sports seasons each year: flag football in the fall and basketball in the spring. name: Splash at Duke
description: Duke Splash is an educational outreach program that aims to spark middle schoolers’ interest and passion towards learning with interactive workshops. Splash’s objective is to show middle schoolers the real world applications of the concepts they learn in class and give them a chance to explore their interests. Splash aims to reach this goal through interactive workshops in STEM and humanities taught by Duke undergraduate students.

name: Spoon University at Duke
description: Spoon is a food community that helps you build your confidence in becoming a real adult. We do this by creating content and experiences for this generation and empowering college students to learn by doing and share that with the world.

name: Stargazing Devils Astronomy Club

description: The mission of the Statistical Sciences Majors’ Union (SSMU) is to foster community within the undergraduate program and connect with members of the wider Duke community who are interested in Statistical Science. SSMU seeks to accomplish this mission by hosting events that encourage relationships between students and professors, supporting ASA DataFest, and hosting panels, workshops and meetings for academic and career development.

name: STEM Pre-Professional and Undergraduate Research Society
description: The missions of SPURS are as follows: - Provide mentorship for undergraduate students pursuing research or graduate school in a STEM field. - Create a community of undergraduate students interested in pursuing research-oriented careers Introduce members to a variety of career and internship options. - Host events with speakers. - Advice students in emailing professors, obtaining laboratory research positions, filling out internship applications, and similar objectives.

name: Stitch by Stitch
description: SBS aims to bring together Duke students of vast interests and connect them in the art of crochet through interactive meetings that allow students to learn how to crochet while building friendships in a positive, supportive environment. We will create handmade gifts, such as hand warmers, mittens, blankets, hats, scarves, and stuffed toys, for residents of Durham homeless shelters (such as Durham Rescue Mission) in order to secure safety and health during cold months. name: Street Medicine
description: Street Medicine is a Duke performance group focused on Hip-Hop/Street-Style dance and culture. By providing a space for Duke students of all skill levels to learn and engage with this culture, Street Medicine seeks to develop a greater interest in street-style dance history and foundations at Duke University, to increase access to dance education and performance opportunities, and to connect interested students with the greater dance and Durham community.

name: Student Advisory Board at the DHRC@FHI
description: The Duke Human Rights Center @ the Franklin Humanities Institute brings together an interdisciplinary group of scholars, staff, and students to promote new understandings of and action on human rights. We engage with issues of race, ethnicity, gender, sexuality, religion, income inequality, the environment, the philosophy and history of human rights, the literature that emerges alongside it, linguistic rights, and artistic responses in our research, teaching, programming, and outreach. description: Student Affairs Staff Resource Office

name: Student Collective at Duke
description: Our mission is to empower Duke students to give back to marginalized communities in Durham through accessible and impactful initiatives. By hosting seasonal drives to collect gently used clothing and essential items, we aim to provide direct support to local nursing homes and rehabilitation centers. Our ultimate vision is to expand this model to other campuses, making giving back simple, meaningful, and far-reaching. GroupMe: https://groupme.com/join_group/109033996/iXYam51T

name: Student Organ Donation Advocates: Undergraduate Chapter at Duke
description: Our mission is to inspire and educate Duke students about organ, eye, and tissue donation and promote donor registration on campus.

description: An independent branch of DSG, SOFC is responsible for the recognition, funding, and support of 350+ student organizations at Duke. In collaboration with campus partners, we work to approve and onboard new groups, ensure the effective distribution and investment of Duke's nearly $1M student fund, and elevate the voices of student leaders. Our goal is to enhance the undergraduate Duke experience by supporting engagement opportunities, student involvement, and inclusive programming.

name: Student Worker Alliance
description: Student & Worker Alliance at Duke seeks to create a space where students can come together to support and elevate the voices of both Duke workers and workers in the Durham and Triangle community. SWA aims to increase awareness and understanding of the many issues and challenges that workers in the Duke and Durham community face. We will also help students translate that knowledge into action by providing transportation to volunteer opportunities to engage with the larger worker community. Another focus of our organization will be to create community among students passionate about labor rights

description: The mission of Duke SJP is to advocate for an end to the occupation of Palestine by the nation of Israel. Duke SJP seeks to accomplish this mission by educating the Duke and Durham communities about what occupation is and by promoting activism in favor of an end to the occupation.

name: Students for Life at Duke
description: Members of this organization will foster open and thoughtful discourse on the ethical, legal, and philosophical dimensions of human life from fertilization to natural death. Students for Life at Duke will create a space for respectful debate, engaging with diverse perspectives on issues such as abortion and end-of-life care. Members will conduct themselves with civility, compassion, and a commitment to promoting dialogue that encourages critical thinking and understanding. name: Students of the Caribbean Association
description: The mission of SOCA is to explore the depths of the rich and shifting cultures of the West Indies. SOCA seeks to accomplish this mission by providing a space for the Duke community to celebrate and learn more about Caribbean culture.

name: Students Providing Aid
description: Spaid Mission: Spaid (Students Providing Aid) is a fully student-run organization dedicated to improving global health by empowering college students to create and distribute child-friendly first aid kits. Focused on helping children in rural and underserved communities worldwide, we aim to close healthcare access gaps through collaboration, education, and strategic partnerships.

name: Students Supporting Israel
description: Our mission is to be a clear and confident pro-Israel voice on college campuses, and to support students in grassroots pro-Israel advocacy. We are committed to promoting a better understanding of Israel throughout North America as a member of the family of nations, with a fundamental right to exist as a Jewish, democratic state, within secure borders. name: Students Taking Action Now
description: The mission of Duke STAND is to facilitate involvement and provide representation for students interested in advocating for human rights, genocide prevention, and global peacebuilding. Duke STAND seeks to accomplish this mission by fostering a tolerant, vibrant, and diverse community that will provide forums for discussing global conflicts and humanitarian crises, facilitating educational initiatives on mass atrocities, organizing advocacy campaigns to promote peace and justice, and actively engaging the surrounding communities through education and civil service. name: Sunrise Duke
description: Un mundo mejor es posible, a better world is possible. Sunrise Duke is building a movement of young people across race and class to protect all workers and students at Duke, organizing towards labor justice, migrant justice, and a new democracy for all, for the people we love and the places we call home. We’re on a mission to dismantle authoritarianism and the billionaire rule of our system, win policies and champions that show up for our communities, and build a world that works for all of us, now and for generations to come.

name: Sustainable Ocean Alliance
description: The mission of SOA is to promote and strengthen student interest, knowledge, and engagement with ocean related research and policy.

name: Swing Dance Team at Duke
description: The purpose of the Duke Swing Dance Club is to provide exposure to the art of swing dancing with regular opportunities to learn, enjoy, and perform swing dancing in a relaxed social setting. In order to accomplish this task, we hold free swing dancing lessons, practice sessions, and events for swing members and occasionally the larger Duke community.

name: Synapse
description: The mission of Synapse is to foster student interest in neuroscience by providing opportunities for students to engage with peers and professionals in the field of neuroscience, and to foster neuroscience interest in the community through service activities. Synapse seeks to accomplish this mission by dinners with neuroscience faculty, events with community students, fundraising and volunteering at Threshold Clubhouse for adults with mental illness.

name: Synergy Dance Company
description: The mission of Synergy Dance Company is to foster a safe space for students of all backgrounds and experience levels to learn and grow as dancers and people. We intend to hold performances throughout the year that showcase all different styles of dance performed by students of various identities to promote diversity and inclusion. description: Duke Taiwanese-American Students Association (TASA) was started with the goal of uniting the Taiwanese and Taiwanese American undergraduate students at Duke University. Since then, we have expanded from a scattered group of a few individuals to a much larger, social circle. We work towards promoting the Taiwanese culture among Duke students as well as providing some comfort for those far away from home. description: The TAMID Group is a nonprofit organization that develops the professional skills of undergraduate students through hands-on interaction with the Israeli economy.

name: Tau Beta Pi
description: Tau Beta Pi seeks to enhance the experience of aspiring engineers of high academic achievement by providing them with the resources necessary to promote change through engineering innovation and philanthropic activity. In addition, Tau Beta Pi strives to augment the experience of all engineering students by hosting a variety of activities to build community within the Pratt School of Engineering.

name: Team One Love at Duke
description: The mission of One Love is to empower Duke students to take action in the movement to end intimate partner violence. One Love seeks to accomplish this mission by facilitating Escalation Workshops and other signature One Love workshops which will allow the Duke community to better understand the mission of the One Love Foundation.

name: Technify

name: TEDxDuke Coordinating Committee
description: The mission of TEDxDuke is to spread ideas worth sharing by hosting an annual conference, alongside partnering with on-campus groups on speaker events throughout the year. TEDxDuke aims to spread ideas that highlight the incredible and diverse work done on campus and will seek to embody this goal by selecting speakers from a broad range of disciplines.

name: Temptasians A Cappella Group
description: The Temptasians is a co-ed a cappella group dedicated to celebrating its members' Asian identities via music from various Asian/Asian American artists.

name: The Alexander Hamilton Society
description: The Hamilton Society will build a national network of these outstanding students and faculty—in effect, a "virtual university"—which will provide its member with vital, constructive debates on foreign, economic, and national security policy, as well as opportunities for students to flourish intellectually, professionally, and personally.

name: The Archive
description: The primary focus of the magazine is the publication of undergraduate student poetry and short fiction. Each edition also showcases photography and artwork. The Archive strives to create a space for artistic and literary expression and to promote the recognition of such exemplary student work.

name: The Backpack Project: Durham
description: The mission of The Backpack Project, Inc, is to pack and hand-deliver backpacks filled with essential supplies; establish a personal connection to uplift each client that we encounter; and connect our clients to other homeless service providers within their community.

name: The Blue Devil Wellness Exchange
description: To provide a springboard for a wide array of wellness techniques, strategies, and activities to aid in the reduction of stressors faced by members of the Duke and Durham community.

name: The Chanticleer
description: The mission of The Chanticleer is to create a yearbook for every academic year. The Chanticleer seeks to accomplish this mission by photographing events and student life throughout the year, organizing an outside agency to take senior portraits, and coordinating with a yearbook publisher to print and distribute the created yearbook.

name: The Coop
description: We are the coop. Duke women deserve greater recognition and representation, and we are here to give it to them. We are committed to creating a supportive, inclusive community of women on and off our campus. In a time where we are separated physically, we want to have a space where we can come together, exchange ideas, and learn from one other. We hope you join us on this journey towards greater female empowerment at Duke.

name: The Duke Alt Protein Project
description: The Duke Alt Protein Project is a student initiative supported by The Good Food Institute. We strive to build a collaborative community of students interested in the future of food by offering educational resources, career support and inter-school networking opportunities.

name: the Duke Darts Corporation
description: The purpose of tDDC is to allow students on campus who are either passionate about the game of darts, or are looking to learn more about the sport, to both practice and play in a friendly, yet competitive, environment. Ultimately, the club seeks to not only allow its members to play against each other, but also against other colleges and local darts teams. description: The English Table is dedicated to creating a vibrant and inclusive conversation space for students with English as their second language—both domestic and international. Through casual conversations, shared meals, and a collaborative learning environment, we aim to accomplish the following: · Provide a supportive community for all levels of English speakers by facilitating cross-cultural connections, fostering unity, and promoting a sense of belonging between domestic and international students at Duke. · Forge union between the Duke English Department and the Duke International Student Center

name: The Flow
description: To uncover advancements, stories, current events, and voices in reproductive health through articles, narratives, research, editorials, and art.

The organization serves to pose as a creative space to facilitate staff writers and editors to produce said content.

description: The mission of Gatekeepers is to organize DevilsGate student football tailgates and increase attendance at football games. The Gatekeepers seeks to accomplish this mission by liaising between the student body and the Duke Athletic staff to compromise on safe and fun events each home game.

description: The mission of TGC is to empower middle school students attending Durham Public Schools, with a specific focus on celebrating the strengths of young women and those who fall outside of the typical gender binary. TGC seeks to accomplish this mission by building a community of mutual trust and respect through weekly meetings between mentees and mentors (Duke undergraduate students who are primarily women) at the Emily K Center, enrichment events in the Durham community, and annual field trips.

name: The Global Energy Access Network
description: We aim to foster a research and policy dialogue around energy access and energy transitions in emerging economies.

name: The Leftist Book Club
description: We believe in the transformative power of literature as a tool for understanding, empathy, and social change. Our book club is committed to selecting a wide range of texts, spanning genres, cultures, and historical periods, that amplify marginalized voices, promote social justice, and encourage dialogue about pressing issues such as economic inequality, racial injustice, gender discrimination, environmental sustainability, and more.

name: The Lemur: Duke's Premier Big Ideas Magazine
description: The Lemur will provide a forum for intellectually ambitious and curious Duke students who wish to share ideas about history, philosophy, politics, art, religion, science, and culture with the broader university community while honing their writing skills with the aid of superb faculty mentorship. The Lemur will be a thought leader on campus, igniting vital discussions about the most vital ethical, political, and cultural questions of our time and all time, and encouraging Duke students to thoughtfully engage with the world and the ideas that shape it. name: The Muse Magazine
description: Our mission is to facilitate an improved culture of women’s and overall gender-informed empowerment on Duke’s campus. We publish monthly volumes for Duke students to explore self-empowerment, journalism, art, poetry, photography, politics, and more. We welcome any individuals as long as they are in support of our mission: the empowerment of women’s voices through writing and art. The Muse is a feminist driven publication at Duke University, founded by two students who desired to create a positive outlet for women’s empowerment on Duke’s campus. description: The Pitchforks are first and foremost a TTBB, a cappella, singing group that performs both on- and off-campus. As an arts organization, we hope to build, hone, and enhance the musical craft of each member that joins the organization. We seek to create a community built upon the pillars of fairness, inclusivity, diversity, camaraderie, and creativity, as well as establish a culture that encourages mutual support between members, so that they can create exceptional music. The Pitchforks are committed to enhancing both students' lives and the lives of Durham community members through performance.

name: The UNICEF Club at Duke University
description: The mission of this organization will be to abide by, uphold, and support the values of the United Nations Children's Fund and to proliferate its values throughout the Duke, Durham, National, and International Communities through education, advocacy, and fundraising efforts.

name: The Wild Ones
description: The mission of The Wild Ones is to provide the Duke community with opportunities to observe nature with a focus on increasing our scientific understanding of and appreciation for the environment. The Wild Ones seeks to accomplish this mission by organizing events including: faculty-led/professional-led naturalist outings with organismal (e.g. insects, plants, birds, reptiles) or ecological (e.g. stream, geology, rare ecosystems) focuses, collections tours, guest lectures, natural arts and crafts, and social events.

name: The Women's Network
description: To create an inclusive community of women that celebrates the desire to achieve, cultivating their ambition in order to prepare the next generation of leaders.

description: The mission of Duke Writers' Collective is to foster a literary culture on campus and make the creative writing process at Duke more dynamic and collaborative. description: The purpose of the Themed Entertainment Association at Duke (TEA) is to foster an interdisciplinary community of students interested in themed entertainment, creative technology, and immersive experiences. The organization aims to bring together students from many backgrounds—engineering, design, storytelling, business, and the arts—to collaborate on hands-on projects and professional development opportunities.

name: Thomistic Institute
description: The mission of the Thomistic Institute at Duke University is to promote academic discussion of the Catholic Church’s intellectual tradition, placing particular emphasis on the thought of the 13th-century philosopher and theologian, Thomas Aquinas. This is done by inviting scholars from other academic institutions to Duke’s campus for lectures on philosophical and theological topics, as well as by hosting theological study groups.

name: Threads of Love and Care
description: At Threads of Love and Care we are dedicated to fostering creativity, compassion, and camaraderie among students while making a meaningful impact on the lives of oncology patients at local hospitals. Our mission is to empower individuals to learn and practice the art of crochet, channeling our collective skills and passion to create and donate handmade items such as hats, scarves, headbands, and more to those bravely facing the challenges of cancer treatment. name: Transfer Students Union
description: The Transfer Student Union will seek to educate and raise awareness for transfer students on Duke's campus. The organization's mission is to improve the transfer integration process and to sustain an engaging transfer community.

name: Triangle Molecular Simulation Society
description: i) To serve as a welcoming and professional community for scientists engaged in the interdisciplinary practice of molecular simulation, encouraging collaboration and career development; ii) To promote molecular simulation in particular, and computational science in general, as an essential pillar of the modern scientific enterprise.

name: Turkish Students Association
description: To bring the Turkish students at Duke together; organize events to share the Turkish culture on campus.

name: TWP Writing Studio
description: The TWP Writing Studio is dedicated to working with writers both within Duke and the broader Durham community. Our goal is to help writers, not just pieces of writing, develop. In all of our work, we actively seek to support diverse, inclusive writing communities. Our highly educated consultants help at any stage of the writing process – from brainstorming and researching to drafting, revising, and fine-tuning a final draft.

name: Undergraduate Environmental Union
description: Our mission is to serve as the hub for all undergraduate environmental activity, communications, and programming at Duke. We partner with environmental clubs, community members, neighboring institutions, Duke faculty members, administrators, university staff, and the larger student body to facilitate conversations and collaboration around sustainability on campus and beyond. name: Undergraduate Law Review at Duke
description: Publish ingenious legal scholarship by undergraduate students with innovative legal research exploring an array of legal disciplines and intersections.

name: Undergraduate Literature Society
description: The Undergraduate Literature Society is a think tank and intellectual support group for establishing and maintaining an undergraduate literature journal housed under the Program in Literature. Our mission is to create a publication exemplifying creative and thoughtful writing about culture, literature, film, and the arts. The journal can be an opportunity for students to engage with cultural theories and contemporary artists/culture makers, to produce new work related to events, ideas, and people. It can also be a chance to publish work from classes, such as creative and/or journalistic writin

name: United Black Athletes
description: The mission of UBA is to form a unified body of Black student-athletes who are committed to advocating for justice and equality in the realm of Duke athletics and the Durham community. UBA is committed to providing a safe space for Black athletes and serving as a bridge between student-athletes and administration. UBA will seek to accomplish this mission by holding general body meetings, mental health events, game nights, guest speakers, and providing service opportunities in the Durham and greater North Carolina communities.

name: United in Praise
description: Relying on God's wisdom, guidance, and sovereignty, United in Praise will minister to the students, faculty, and staff of Duke University as well as the Durham community via song.

name: United Students for Veterans' Health at Duke
description: Connecting students with veterans through service, compassion, and clinical volunteering at the Durham VA.

name: Venture Group at Duke
description: Duke Venture Group (DVG) is Duke University's premier, student-run venture capital organization—offering a hands-on experience for undergraduates to engage in the sourcing, evaluation, and strategic support of early-stage startups. Through a partnership with Duke's Innovation and Entrepreneurship department, DVG operates at the intersection of entrepreneurship and finance, providing students with unparalleled access to venture capitalists, real-world diligence processes, and the Duke startup ecosystem.

name: Vertices
description: Vertices is a student-run online science magazine and undergraduate research journal that aims to highlight groundbreaking scientific research and news at Duke and beyond. Composed of writers, editors, peer reviewers, artists, website designers, and more, our interdisciplinary team believes science should be accessible and exciting to everyone.

name: Vietnamese Student Association
description: The Duke Vietnamese Student Association seeks to connect, advocate for, and uplift the Vietnamese community here at Duke. We hope to foster and share an appreciation of Vietnamese culture to the community at-large.

name: Visions of Freedom Living Learning Community
description: To unite students at Duke University who share a common passion for politics, philosophy, and economics in an immersive living and learning community; To foster a vibrant intellectual space where the political, philosophical, and economic issues of today may be discussed and debated among all students; To expand general student interest and knowledge of political, philosophical, and economic principles and their manifestation in the world today.

name: Wesley Campus Ministry

name: West Campus Council
description: The West Campus Council represents and contributes to the residential experience of all students on West Campus.

name: Wingman's Society

name: WISER Duke
description: WISER is located in Muhuru Bay, Kenya and works to empower girls to transcend poverty, HIV/AIDS, and gender-based violence through education.

name: Women in Entrepreneurship at Duke
description: Duke's premier women in entrepreneurship group designed to help you ship. This isn't a place where you'll just *think* about an idea. You'll take it from 0 to 1 and meet incredible people along the way. Don't worry, you don't need a technical background to start. And if you are technical, we've got so much for you too! We will provide everything you need to learn and collaborate. All you have to do is show up with energy, creativity, and ready to go go go.

name: Women in National Security at Duke
description: The mission of Duke Women in National Security is to create a supportive space for women to discuss national security and cyber issues, tackle the unique challenges we face, and cultivate the next generation of female leaders in this field.

name: Women in Science & Engineering
description: Women in Science and Engineering (WiSE) originated from several women-in-science initiatives sponsored at the university from 1989 through 1993. At that time, students, faculty, and administrators agreed that Duke needed to accomplish two goals: increase the number of women faculty members and students in science and engineering and provide programmatic support for open discussion of science and gender issues. name: Women In Technology
description: The mission of Women in Tech is to build and strengthen a community of women and nonbinary individuals in computing, provide educational and professional opportunities, and raise awareness around the issues women and nonbinary individuals in the field face. Women in Tech seeks to accomplish this mission by creating supportive networks between women and nonbinary individuals in computer science, and collaborating with industry professionals to provide opportunities for learning and growth.

name: Women's Empowerment at Duke
description: The mission of WE@Duke is to empower, educate, and advocate for gender equity and women's empowerment through facilitated discussions, community building and engagement, and guest speaker events. We work with all members of the Duke community, no matter their gender identity.

name: Women's Wellness Club
description: The mission of WWC is to allow female identifying students at duke to connect and grow on an emotional level while developing healthy wellness strategies and bonding with many students of different interests and backgrounds.

name: Womxn of Color Collective
description: The Womxn of Color Collective (WOCC) at Duke Law seeks to provide a supportive community space for Asian & Pacific Islander, Black, Latinx, Middle Eastern/North African, Native American, and other women and trans people of color. We are open to engaging with all people ready to participate in an open and honest dialogue about race, gender and the law. Our mission is to promote the empowerment, inspiration, and personal and professional development of womxn and people of color in the legal field.

name: Working Group on the Environment in Latin America
description: WGELA aims to 1) foster a dialogue concerning critical environmental issues affecting Latin America, 2) improve the understanding of the social, historical, political, and cultural contexts in which these environmental issues are embedded, and 3) build capacity among an interdisciplinary and cross-institutional group of individuals to address and conduct research on Latin American issues.

name: Wushu at Duke
description: The mission of the Duke Kung Fu & Wushu Club is to preserve, practice, and promote the art of wushu (traditional Chinese martial arts); to expand its knowledge and cultural significance at the collegiate level; to train students in the fundamentals of both traditional and competitive wushu; and to inspire lifelong dedication to the discipline. Through training, performance, and competition at the regional, national, and international levels, we seek to uphold the legacy of this martial arts tradition while fostering a community of committed practitioners.

name: WXDU Durham
description: WXDU, as a member of the Duke University Union, exists to inform, educate, and entertain both the students of Duke University and the surrounding community of Durham through quality progressive alternative radio programming. WXDU seeks to give its staff the freedom to pursue their personal aesthetic within the framework of a cohesive format.

name: Zeta Phi Beta Sorority, Inc.
description: It is the mission of the Nu Omicron Chapter to uphold the tenets of scholarship, service, sisterly love, and FINER WOMANHOOD on which Zeta Phi Beta Sorority, Inc. was founded. We continue to advance our sorority's impact on the world by building on the traditions of our past while addressing the concerns of contemporary society in the Duke and Durham, North Carolina communities.
